- Why is MD1 still at 26GeV - I think for new MDs
- Why is the injection bump removed in SFTPRO
- Has it been shortened?

Answers (sent to Alberto via email):

**Why has MD1 been shortened to 2BPs ->** Actually, it's still 3BPs, but (then and now) the magnets are only pulsed for about 2BPs, which is why we thought it was shortened just from reading page 1. This is what the programmed momentum looks like in LSA for full MD1 and flat MD1 respectively. You can see that it ends around 2600ms. LSA will then automatically interpolate a ramp-down to 14GeV and play that until the start of the next cycle at 3600ms. Of course, this new ramp-down doesn't take as long as the old one, since it's coming from 26GeV instead of from 200 --- in that sense the total 'pulse time' is indeed slightly shorter.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

**Why doesn't SFTPRO have the injection plateau ->** Apparently it never had this either. For some reason, I really thought that it had a 26GeV plateau like MD1 and MD5, but I guess not 🤷‍♂️

**Why is MD1 still going to 26GeV? Why not just zeroes? ->** This is for parallel machine development studies. The beam will not be injected on MD1 specifically, but on other MD cycles which are slightly longer* and but which are also at a flat 26GeV. As such, it's convenient to keep MD1 ramping to 26GeV as well because then one can swap it in and out for other MD cycles without effecting the hysteresis of the subsequent SFTPRO (disregarding differences in eddies of course).

*  The parallel MD cycles used to be 6BPs, but part of that included an MD1-like ramp which has now been removed. As such, those where actually able to be shorted to 4BPs. A nice side-effect of this study!
